newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 26.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 26.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

A soccer-style red and yellow card system will be introduced in this year's Super 12 Rugby Union and Tri-nation series in an effort to curb foul play, professional fouls and repeat offenders. A sin bin, where players cool-off for 10 minutes, will also be introduced with approval from the International Rugby Board. Page 20.

North Melbourne's ruckman Matthew Capuano will miss the entire Australian Football League season as he needs a knee reconstruction. His injury is a severe blow to North Melbourne and Capuano, as the club have an active list of just 38 players, four below the maximum. Page 20.

The board of the New South Wales Rugby League, which runs the Australian Rugby League's Optus Cup competition, was considering increasing the size of the competition from 12 to 14 teams next season. The increase would involve new clubs in Melbourne and eiher Adelaide or New Zealand. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Industry sources say Lion Nathan is about to end its five-year association with the New South Wales State of Origin team. The move would be a significant blow to the Australian Rugby League, and it is unclear whether Lion Nathan (Toohey's parent company) will drop its sponsorship of the Queensland State of Origin team. Page 46.

A Federal Court ruling means cricket fans will be able to watch live free-to-air coverage of at least half of each day's play in Australia's first test against South Africa from Friday. Justice John Lockhart yesterday ruled pay-TV services could not acquire rights to televise major sporting events live when only highlight packages were being shown on free-to-air television. Page 46.

Adelaide AFL captain Tony McGuiness and his manager are expected to lodge an affidavit or statutory declaration with the Australian Football League today, offering their version of the alleged attempts by the Sydney Swans to pre-arrange his drafting. The Swans may know late today whether they face further investigation by the AFL. Page 45.
THE AGE

Poor funding may force award-winning swimming coach John Carew to sell his distance-coaching expertise to Japan or the United States. Carew coaches Australian Olympic swimming champion Kieren Perkins, and received A$7500 from Swimming Australia last year. Page C20.

The Australian Football League will inform clubs of a decision on the proposed Docklands Stadium at a special summit to be called next Monday or Tuesday. North Melbourne chairman Ron Casey said his club opposed the stadium at the club's annual meeting last night and gained some support from Hawthorn president Ian Dicker. Page C20.

Arrowfield stud formally announced yesterday it was transferring a large part of its operation from New South Wales to Victoria. The move highlights the growing turmoil in the NSW racing industry, which has been long regarded as the headquarters of Austraia's horse breeding industry. Page C18.
THE HERALD SUN

Essendon's James Hird is likely to become the Australian Football League's highest paid player as his management begin negotiations for a new three-year contract. Hird is expected to earn up to A$500,000 a season and has the capacity to earn A$300,000 a year in endorsements. Page 80.

Australian cyclists Brett Aitken and Stephen Pate will team for the first time in Saturday's A$10,000 Australian madison title. The madison is one of two selection races for the world championships, and the pair are hoping a good performance at the world itles could lead to a contract for the six-day circuit. Page 68.

Soccer Australia has announced that a 12, 14 or 16 team Ericsson Cup competition format is being considered for the national league's 21st season. Three teams could be thrown out because of the expense associated with a 16 or 14 team competition. Page 73.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

New South Wales Minister for Gaming and Racing Richard Face attacked senior racing administrators in response to strike threats in the State. Face said the strike plan was part of a master plan to embarrass the Government into giving the A$4 billion racing industry in NSW taxation relief. Page 80.

Australian golfer Karrie Webb said she aims to win a major and become Player of the Year as she prepared for the A$850,000 Alpine Australian Ladies Masters at Royal Pines starting tomorrow. Webb, 22, became the first woman in history to win US$1 million in a single season. Page 74.

Australian soccer's European-based players were put through their paces by coach Terry Venables at the start of a three-day training camp in London. Soccer Australia chairman David Hill is to visit FA chief executive Graham Kelly this week to arrange a friendly between the two countries. Page 75.
